name: Accurate Online
tagline: Cloud accounting, inventory and tax reporting software built for Indonesian businesses.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: You can absolutely one-shot a double-entry ledger: accounts, journals, a trial balance, a P and L. What you cannot one-shot is Indonesian tax conformance, which is the entire reason people buy this thing. Accurate exists to emit invoices, VAT reports and withholding data that survive contact with DJP rules and with whatever the tax office changed this quarter, plus the inventory and multi-branch bookkeeping an operating business actually runs on. Your accountant also knows this software, and the chart of accounts, reports and audit trail they expect are not a weekend of prompting. A personal ledger for tracking your own freelance income is a fine build; a replacement for a company's books is not.
coreLoopDIY: A local double-entry ledger that records invoices and expenses, computes VAT at a configurable rate, and prints a trial balance, P and L and balance sheet.
requirements: Your own chart of accounts, hand written once
Enough accounting literacy to know when a report is wrong
An actual accountant for anything you file
whatYouLose: Tax conformance: VAT invoicing, withholding and whatever the current e-invoicing regime demands
Inventory, costing methods, multi warehouse and multi branch bookkeeping
An audit trail and report set your accountant already recognises
Bank feeds, payroll and the marketplace or POS integrations most users depend on
Someone else being responsible when the numbers are wrong
moatNotes: The hardest part is not the ledger math, it is tracking a regulator that keeps moving and having accountants trust your output.
whyPeopleStillPay: Accounting software is bought for liability transfer as much as for features. A business pays so that invoices are formatted the way the tax office wants, so VAT and withholding land in the right boxes, and so the external accountant opens the file and immediately knows where everything is. All of that is regulatory and social, not technical. A self built ledger is fine for a solo freelancer who just wants to see cash in and cash out, and indefensible for anyone who files returns, carries stock, or has staff.
notes: The double-entry engine is a weekend; the compliance surface is a permanent job. The moat is Indonesian tax conformance plus every accountant already knowing this software.
prompt:
Build a local-first personal double-entry bookkeeping app. Stack: Next.js 14 App Router, TypeScript, Prisma with SQLite, Tailwind. No auth, no cloud, no telemetry. Single user on localhost.

Data model:
- Account: code, name, type (asset, liability, equity, income, expense), active flag
- Party: customer or vendor, name, tax id optional
- Transaction: date, memo, reference, plus JournalLine rows (account, debit, credit) that must balance to zero before save
- Invoice: party, issue date, due date, line items (description, qty, unit price), configurable tax rate percent, status (draft, sent, paid)
- Payment: links to an invoice, date, amount, account credited

Behaviour:
- Seed a small default chart of accounts on first run, editable
- Posting an invoice or payment generates the journal entry automatically; everything is still visible and editable as raw journal lines
- Reject any transaction where debits do not equal credits, with a clear error
- Reports, all with a date range picker: trial balance, profit and loss, balance sheet, accounts receivable aging, and a tax summary listing invoice tax collected versus expense tax paid
- CSV export for every report and a full JSON backup and restore
- Print stylesheet so an invoice detail page prints cleanly as PDF via the browser

Explicitly out of scope: multi currency, inventory and costing, payroll, bank feeds, government e-invoicing or any tax authority integration, multi user roles.

Deliver: prisma schema, seed script, the pages, a README with setup commands, and a clear note in the README that this output is not suitable for statutory filing.
